ei.title: The Fallacy of Composition in Teamwork
ei.subject: 6월_2026 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: The Fallacy of Composition in Teamwork

fullPassage: We can sometimes assume that the whole will be as good as each of its parts. Suppose, for example, you're in charge of a startup, and you know that everyone you've brought on board is productive and efficient. It might seem logical to assume that, as a result, the startup will be productive and efficient, too — but this isn't necessarily true. The fallacy of composition fails to allow for how the different "parts" interact with each other — if, for example, your efficient administrator and your highly skilled head of IT each assumes the other is in charge of collating prototype test results, then you have a problem. Equally, a unit composed of good people can still be working on a doomed project, and a project composed of good ideas may lack a stable center. When assembling a team with a common goal, always check the overall view as well as the individuals involved.

questions.passage: We can sometimes assume that the whole will be as good as each of its parts. Suppose, for example, you're in charge of a startup, and you know that everyone you've brought on board is (A)[productive / lazy] and (B)[efficient / wasteful]. It might seem logical to assume that, as a result, the startup will be productive and efficient, too — but this isn't necessarily true. The fallacy of composition fails to allow for how the different "parts" interact with each other — if, for example, your efficient administrator and your highly skilled head of IT each assumes the other is in charge of collating prototype test results, then you have a problem. Equally, a unit composed of good people can still be working on a doomed project, and a project composed of good ideas may lack a (C)[stable / chaotic] center. When assembling a team with a common goal, always check the overall view as well as the individuals involved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① lazy(게으른) — efficient — stable: lazy가 틀림. 생산적(productive)
❌ ② productive — wasteful(낭비적인) — stable: wasteful이 틀림. 효율적(efficient)
❌ ③ productive — efficient — chaotic(혼란스러운): chaotic이 틀림. 안정적(stable)
✅ ④ productive(생산적) — efficient(효율적) — stable(안정적): 원문 일치 ← 정답

questions.passage: We can sometimes (A)[assume / deny] that the whole will be as good as each of its parts. Suppose, for example, you're in charge of a startup, and you know that everyone you've brought on board is productive and efficient. It might seem logical to assume that, as a result, the startup will be productive and efficient, too — but this isn't necessarily true. The fallacy of composition fails to allow for how the different "parts" (B)[interact / separate] with each other — if, for example, your efficient administrator and your highly skilled head of IT each assumes the other is in charge of collating prototype test results, then you have a problem. Equally, a unit composed of good people can still be working on a doomed project, and a project composed of good ideas may lack a stable center. When assembling a team with a common goal, always check the (C)[overall / partial] view as well as the individuals involved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① deny(부인하다): 가정하다(assume)가 원문
✅ ② assume + interact + overall: 원문 일치 ← 정답
❌ ③ separate(분리하다): 상호작용하다(interact)가 원문
❌ ④ partial(부분적인): 전체적인(overall)이 원문

questions.passage: We can sometimes assume that the whole will be as good as each of its parts. Suppose, for example, you're in charge of a startup, and you know that everyone you've brought on board is productive and efficient. It might seem logical to assume that, as a result, the startup will be productive and efficient, too — but this isn't necessarily true. The (A)[fallacy / truth] of composition fails to allow for how the different "parts" interact with each other — if, for example, your efficient administrator and your highly skilled head of IT each assumes the other is in charge of collating prototype test results, then you have a problem. Equally, a unit composed of good people can still be working on a (B)[doomed / successful] project, and a project composed of good ideas may lack a stable center. When (C)[assembling / dismantling] a team with a common goal, always check the overall view as well as the individuals involved.

❌ ② truth(진실): 오류(fallacy)가 원문
❌ ③ successful(성공적인): 실패할(doomed) 프로젝트가 원문
❌ ④ dismantling(해체하는): 구성하는(assembling)이 원문

questions.passage: We can sometimes ①<u>assume</u> that the whole will be as good as each of its parts. Suppose, for example, you're in charge of a startup, and you know that everyone you've brought on board is ②<u>productive</u> and efficient. It might seem ③<u>absurd</u> to assume that, as a result, the startup will be productive and efficient, too — but this isn't necessarily true. The fallacy of composition fails to allow for how the different "parts" ④<u>interact</u> with each other — if, for example, your efficient administrator and your highly skilled head of IT each assumes the other is in charge of collating prototype test results, then you have a problem. Equally, a unit composed of good people can still be working on a doomed project, and a project composed of good ideas may lack a stable center. When assembling a team with a common goal, always check the overall view as well as the individuals involved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ absurd → logical: 논리적으로 보일 수 있다가 원문
det.analysis:
✅ ① assume(가정하다): 전체가 부분만큼 좋을 것이라 가정 — 적절
✅ ② productive(생산적인): 모두 생산적이고 효율적 — 적절
❌ ③ absurd(터무니없는): 원문은 logical(논리적인). 논리적으로 보이지만 반드시 그렇지 않다는 문맥 ← 정답
✅ ④ interact(상호작용하다): 부분들이 어떻게 상호작용하는지 — 적절

questions.passage: We can sometimes assume that the whole will be as good as each of its parts. Equally, a unit ③<u>composed</u> of good people can still be working on a ④<u>thriving</u> project, and a project composed of good ideas may lack a stable center. det.korean: ④ thriving → doomed: 좋은 사람들로 구성된 팀도 실패할(doomed) 프로젝트에 있을 수 있다
det.analysis:
✅ ① startup(스타트업): 스타트업을 담당 — 적절

✅ ③ composed(구성된): 좋은 사람들로 구성된 — 적절
❌ ④ thriving(번창하는): 원문 doomed(실패할). 좋은 팀이라도 실패할 프로젝트에 있을 수 있다는 역설 ← 정답
